_doc: One run of the serving survey. Keys are (host, backend, label); the same weights served by two engines are two instruments, so they are two entries. `family` is a CLAIM that they are the same model — the digests decide, and may refute it.

models.label: q15-ollama-srv1
models._expect_note: expect.model_sha256 pins the weights: a tag is mutable, and the same name re-pulled serves different bytes while every other check still passes. Obtained by running once without it and reading the digest off the description.

concurrency._expect_note: No `expect`: this engine has no recoverable batch width. The throughput plateau alone returned 6 for two hosts configured one slot apart (-np 2 and -np 1), and there is no latency plateau at any width, so `knee` correctly reports None. An expectation here would be permanently unmeetable.

models.label: q15-vllm-s8

serve._bytes_per_token_note: 28 layers x 2 KV heads x 128 head_dim x 2 (K and V) x 2 bytes (fp16) = 28,672 B/token. Confirmed against vLLM's own allocation on 2026-08-22: 3.5 GiB over 131,104 tokens is 28,665 B/token, the shortfall being block padding. ADR-0039.
serve._footprint_note: MEASURED on the cards 2026-08-22, not computed -- the arithmetic predicts the KV cache and only nvidia-smi says what the process took. Under the withdrawn gpu_memory_utilization 0.85 the same entry took 4916 MiB on srv1 and 10197 MiB on srv2 while reaching the same 65,536 KV tokens.

models._expect_note: sha256 over every tensor's bytes in the checkpoint, in sorted key order across all shards, computed on the serving host — this engine states no weights digest on any endpoint. Measured on srv1: 731 tensors, 1.61 GB, 5.1s. NOT comparable with another backend's digest, which is why the field is named apart.
